lessons.title: Changes in relationships
objectives: Describe an experience or change in a familiar relationship.
Develop a connected response in a discussion about changes in relationships with a reason and relevant detail.

content_sections.title: Notice the connected language (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read this model: 'I have considered changes in relationships, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.' Identify the main point, the linking expression, and the supporting detail. Then explain how the wording helps the speaker achieve this objective: Describe an experience or change in a familiar relationship.

content_sections.title: Guided exchange (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work with a partner in a discussion about changes in relationships. Give a clear main point, support it with a specific reason, and respond to one follow-up question. Use tactful language when the other speaker presents a different perspective.

content_sections.title: Independent connected response (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Prepare a one-minute response about changes in relationships. Organize it into thought groups, stress the words that carry your main point, and finish with a concise conclusion rather than a list of isolated sentences.

exercises.prompt: Choose the most connected and tactful response for a discussion about changes in relationships.
options: I have considered changes in relationships, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
Changes in relationships is a topic, but I will not explain my view.
Several details exist about changes in relationships, perhaps.
exercises.correct_answer: I have considered changes in relationships, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.

exercises.prompt: Complete this response about changes in relationships: 'My experience supports this view ____.'
acceptable_answers: because it offers evidence about changes in relationships

exercises.prompt: Read the short response about changes in relationships and identify how the writer handles another view.
exercises.stimulus: Although another person may disagree about changes in relationships, I can respond politely and explain my reason.

questions.question: How does the writer respond to disagreement?
acceptable_answers: The writer responds politely and gives a reason in the discussion of changes in relationships.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 60–90 seconds in a discussion about changes in relationships. State your point, support it, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Presents a connected main point about changes in relationships with relevant support.
Responds clearly and tactfully to a follow-up question about changes in relationships.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short response about changes in relationships. Identify the view and supporting reason before the transcript is revealed, then listen again to check the linking language.
listening.goal: Follow the main point and support in spoken language about changes in relationships.
listening.transcript: I have considered changes in relationships, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
listening.question: What view and supporting reason does the speaker communicate?
listening.answer: The speaker connects a considered view about changes in relationships to a useful reason from experience.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay a discussion about changes in relationships. Learner role: present and support a view. Tutor role: ask one probing question and offer a different perspective. End after the learner responds tactfully and summarizes the point.
speaking.goal: Sustain a connected, tactful exchange about changes in relationships.
constraints: State both roles before beginning the exchange.
Use at most four tutor turns and stop after the learner summary.

pronunciation.instruction: Record the model about changes in relationships in meaningful thought groups. Stress the main point and reason, then compare a second attempt with the first for clarity and rhythm.
pronunciation.goal: Make connected speech about changes in relationships easy to follow.
pronunciation.target: Thought groups and information stress for changes in relationships
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write 90–120 words about changes in relationships. State a position or experience, support it with a reason and example, and acknowledge another perspective. Submit your own draft before asking for feedback.
writing.goal: Produce a connected written response about changes in relationships.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
